memory_update.text: CRWV and NBIS are direct public AI-cloud capacity plays for the hyperscaler/AI compute-demand node; monitor customer concentration, contracted power, funding and utilization rather than treating revenue growth alone as proof of bottleneck capture.
FIX and MOD are second-order infrastructure suppliers tied to the physical conversion of AI capex into deployable clusters; backlog, data-center mix and margin resilience are the key evidence gates.

BE is a higher-risk chokepoint candidate because onsite power is highly relevant to grid-constrained AI data centers, but commercial adoption, permitting, financing and fuel economics need stronger validation.

node: Hyperscaler, AI cloud and sovereign AI compute demand
summary: Expanded the universe around scarce capacity and deployment bottlenecks for hyperscaler, AI-cloud and sovereign compute demand. The strongest incremental candidates are direct AI-cloud capacity providers and second-order physical-infrastructure suppliers tied to power, cooling, mechanical/electrical construction and onsite generation. This pass intentionally avoids buy/sell conclusions and treats each name as a research candidate requiring customer, backlog, margin and deployment-timing verification.
